newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP attacks EU Dublin reform proposals.
newsitem.headline: EP attacks EU Dublin reform proposals.

text.p: The European Parliament said on Wednesday that proposals for reforming the European Union, which EU leaders will examine at the Dublin summit on December 13-14, were "deeply disappointing" and "insufficient".

The Euro-MPs said the Irish EU Presidency had done "the best it could" in drafting an outline revision of the EU treaties for the Dublin summit to consider this weekend, in the face of disagreements between the EU member states.

But they complained that the document was deeply disappointing, criticising it for not proposing reforms of the EU institutions and for lacking ambition on "essential questions" like the extension of qualified majority voting.
Euro-MPs urged the EU heads of state and government to take crucial decisions on EU treaty reform, monetary union and Europe's foreign policy at the summit.

"The European Parliament makes a formal appeal to the European Council...to take those essential decisions capable of creating the economic, political and social conditions necessary to give a fresh impetus to the Union and bring it closer to its citizens," Euro-MPs said in a resolution.
Parliament asked the summit to take steps to ensure the smooth introduction of the single European currency in 1999 and the creation of lasting jobs.
EU leaders should refrain from imposing rigid budgetary constraints on member states in the forthcoming stability pact, Euro-MPs said.

As for the EU's role on the world stage, the Parliament said the Irish presidency's proposals were "totally insufficient to provide the Union with instruments to be able to create an authentic common foreign and defence policy."

The EU's incapacity to participate in conflict prevention in places like Rwanda and Zaire was deplorable and pointed to the need for a more coherent and coordinated response in external affairs, the Parliament said.
